channel.title: The Batch | DeepLearning.AI
channel.description: Weekly AI news for engineers, executives, and enthusiasts

item.title: Undressed Images Spur Regulators: X rolls back Grok’s “spicy” image generation on the platform after global outrage
item.description: Governments worldwide sounded alarms after xAI’s Grok chatbot generated tens of thousands of sexualized images of girls and women without their consent.

item.title: AI Giants Vie for Healthcare Dollars: OpenAI and Anthropic release new chatbots targeting medical and wellness markets
item.description: OpenAI and Anthropic staked claims in the lucrative healthcare market, each company playing to its strengths by targeting different audiences.

item.title: Meta Moves to Buy Agent Tech: Meta strikes a deal to acquire Manus, a Singapore-based agentic AI startup with Chinese origins
item.description: A high-profile acquisition could enable Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp to offer built-in agents that do users’ bidding.

item.title: Retrieval Faces Hard Limits: Google and Johns Hopkins researchers show embedding models can’t search unlimited documents
item.description: Can your retriever find all the relevant documents for any query your users might enter? Maybe not, research shows.

item.title: Data Centers Are More Easier on the Environment Than You Might Think: How environmentally friendly are AI data centers? If we're going to use AI, there’s no better way to do it.
item.description: Many people are fighting the growth of data centers because they could increase CO2 emissions, electricity prices, and water use.

item.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Go worldwide: Anthropic sees AI failure as an economic bottleneck
item.description: GLM-Image, an open-weights hybrid image model. TranslateGemma, Google’s fast translation model. Wikipedia’s new partnerships with AI companies. FLUX.2 [klein], a noncommercial image model for consumer hardware.

item.title: An AI system to identify teen ChatGPT users: GLM-4.7-Flash, a top 30B parameter model, is free to use
item.description: Persona drift: how prompts can enable bad behavior. X’s transformer-based personalization algorithm. How Cursor agents built a working web browser in a week. Expanding ChatGPT and model access for students.

item.title: Self-Driving Reasoning Models, ChatGPT Adds Ads, Apple’s Deal with Google, 3D Generation Pronto
item.description: The Batch AI News and Insights: How can businesses go beyond using AI for incremental efficiency gains to create transformative impact?

item.title: From AI Experiments to AI Products: Experiemental projects can reveal AI powered-opportunities, but building AI-powered products often requires redesigning workflows.
item.description: How can businesses go beyond using AI for incremental efficiency gains to create transformative impact?

item.title: ChatGPT Shows Ads: OpenAI tests advertisements for U.S. chatbot users in free and lower-cost tiers
item.description: AI has a new revenue stream, and it looks a lot like old web banner ads.

item.title: Training Cars to Reason: Nvidia’s Alpamayo-R1 is a robotics-style reasoning model for autonomous vehicles
item.description: Chain-of-thought reasoning can help autonomous vehicles decide what to do next.

item.title: Apple’s Foundation Models Will Be Gemini: Apple announced a partnership with Google to power Siri and other AI features
item.description: Apple cut a multi-year deal with Google to use Gemini models as the basis of AI models that reside on Apple devices.

item.title: Detailed Text- or Image-to-3D, Pronto: FlashWorld generates 3D objects, scenes, and surfaces with photorealistic fidelity
item.description: Current methods that produce 3D scenes from text or images are slow and produce inconsistent results. Researchers introduced a technique that generates detailed, coherent 3D scenes seconds.

item.title: Anthropic updates Claude’s founding document: AI companies are obsessed with one video game
item.description: LFM2.5-1.2B-Thinking, a smartphone-sized reasoning model. Adobe’s initiative to win over the movie business. Google’s partnership with Japan’s biggest startup. AI companies’ relationship reset with U.S. government.

item.title: Moonshot lands a big one with Kimi K2.5: Qwen releases its own giant flagship reasoning model
item.description: OpenAI’s move to win over scientists and scholars. How U.S. workers are adopting (and not adopting) AI. Moltbot, an open-source local automation agent. Nvidia’s latest open weather and climate models.
